sentences.text: With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants / claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 4/5/2023 passed in MCC.No.29/2021 by the Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rajgarh (Biaora) whereby a total sum of Rs.9,84,200/- has been awarded to them by way of compensation.
3. As per the appellants on 14/6/2020 Rakesh Kumar Verma, husband of appellant No.1, father of appellant No.2 and son of appellants No.3 and 4 had gone in an ambulance to Government Hospital Rajgarh.

While coming back at about 8.00 PM the ambulance was dashed by a Bolero car bearing registration No.M.P. 04 CP 9829 which was being driven by respondent No.1 and was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured by respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6126 2 MA-5637-2023 No.3.
As a result of the accident Rakesh suffered grievous injuries and was taken for treatment to the hospital and eventually expired.
4. Thereafter the appellants have filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the claims tribunal for award of compensation to them on account of death of Rakesh.
The application was contested by the non-applicants by filing their written statement to the same.

After evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded compensation to Khushbu vs Nasruddin Kha on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133752415/
1 the appellants as aforesaid.

5. This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellants on the ground that the income of the deceased which was taken at Rs.4000/- per month by the claims tribunal is extremely low.
The deceased was a driver and at the time of accident itself was driving the ambulance.
He was in regular employment hence his income could not have been taken to be at paltry amount of Rs.4000/-.
It is further submitted that the amount of filial consortium has been granted to only one of the appellant whereas the same ought to have been awarded individually to all the appellants.
It is hence submitted that the amount of compensation awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellants in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6126 3 MA-5637-2023 8.
At the time of the accident the deceased was driving the vehicle which was an ambulance.
Though it is stated that he was a driver but no documents have been produced before the claims tribunal to prove the said fact.
However the fact remains that he was driving the vehicle and even if he was not in regular employment then also he has to be considered as a semi skilled labour.

Considering the fact that the accident took place in the year 2020, even as per the guidelines issued by the Labour Department of the State Government, the income of semi skilled labour ought to have been assessed at Rs.8000/- per month.

The amount which the appellants would be entitled for under the head of loss of dependency would hence be Rs.8000/- + 40% for future prospects of rise in income multiplied by 12 for making it annually.
The deduction of 1/4th and multiplier of 18 applied by the claims tribunal is correct.
The amount for loss of dependency is hence worked out at 18,14,400/-.
9. The appellants are four in number and are the wife, child and parents of the deceased.
In view of the decision of the Apex Court Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd.

V/s. Nanuram @ Chuhru Ram &
Others, 2018 18 SCC 130 each of them deserves to be awarded filial consortium.
The appellants would hence be entitled for a total sum of Rs.1,76,000/- under the head of filial consortium.
10. The appellants are entitled for a total sum of Rs.20,23,400/- to them by way of compensation whereas the claims tribunal has awarded them a sum of Rs.9,84,200/- only.

The appellants are hence held entitled for enhanced amount of compensation in the sum of Rs.10,39,200/- which shall NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6126 4 MA-5637-2023 be payable to them along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.

2 11.
The appellants have valued this appeal at Rs.6,00,000/- whereas the enhancement has been made in the sum of Rs.10,39,200/-.
The appellants shall hence be liable to pay the requisite Court fees for the difference amount of Rs.4,39,200/- which shall be paid by them before this Court within a period of two months.
In case of failure of the appellants to pay the Court fees as aforesaid, the said amount of Rs.4,39,200/- shall cease to carry any interest after a period of two months.
12. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE SS/-
